record.original_question: Suppose B is a subgroup of the symmetric group S_Ω on an infinite set Ω. Will the amalgamated free product S_Ω*_B S_Ω of two copies of S_Ω with amalgamation of B be embeddable in S_Ω? This is a weakened form of the group case of Question 4.4 in(G. M. Bergman, Indag. Math., 18(2007), 349–403). It is known that S_Ω*_B S_Ω need not be so embeddable by a map respecting B(Algebra Number Theory, 3(2009), 847–879, § 10).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega$ be an infinite set and let $S_\Omega$ denote the symmetric group on $\Omega$ (the group of all bijections $\Omega \to \Omega$). Let $B$ be a subgroup of $S_\Omega$, and form the amalgamated free product $S_\Omega *_B S_\Omega$ of two copies of $S_\Omega$ amalgamated along the common subgroup $B$. 

Question: Does there always exist a group embedding $S_\Omega *_B S_\Omega \hookrightarrow S_\Omega$?

(Note: It is known that there need not exist such an embedding whose restriction to $B$ is the identity, i.e., one respecting the amalgamated subgroup $B$. The question asks only whether some embedding into $S_\Omega$ exists, without requiring it to respect $B$.)
artifact.category_tag: Infinite symmetric groups and amalgamated products
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question. Related work by Bergman and by Hodges/Shelah-style constructions addresses embeddings respecting the amalgamated subgroup (known to fail in general), but no source confirms a positive or negative answer to the weaker embeddability question without the requirement of respecting B. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.
